about: The prayer begins by asking God to remember His servants and handmaids. The priest then joins his hands and prays in silence for those he intends to name. The prayer then embraces all who are present and names its intentions: the redemption of their souls, the hope of salvation, and their well-being.

seg.tr: Remember, O Lord, Your servants, both men and women

fn.w004: Genitive plural with the conjunction “-que” attached.

seg.nr: The priest joins his hands and prays a while in silence for those he means to remember, then spreads his hands and goes on.

seg.tr: and all who are here present, whose faith is known to You and whose devotion is clear to You; for them we offer You

fn.w008: A participle used as a noun in the genitive plural.
fn.w013: The shared verb of “fides cognita” and “nota devótio”.

seg.tr: — or they themselves offer You — this sacrifice of praise for themselves and all their own: for the redemption of their souls, in hope of their salvation and well-being;

fn.w027: The phrase “sacrifícium laudis” occurs in Ps 49:14 and 106:22.
fn.w029: “pro” (w028) requires the ablative. The form “se” itself marks neither number nor gender.
fn.w030: Ablative plural after “pro” (w028), with the conjunction “-que” attached.
fn.w033: Ablative after “pro” (w032): “for the redemption of their souls”.
fn.w038: A genitive dependent on “spe” (w037), coordinated with “incolumitátis” (w040).

seg.tr: and fulfill their vows to You, the eternal, living, and true God.

fn.w043: The phrase “vota réddere” occurs in Ps 115:14 and 18.
fn.w047: Dative marking the recipient of the vows. The phrase “Deo vivo et vero” occurs in 1 Thess 1:9.
